intent.purpose: Per-tool operational metadata for managed tools with deep harness integration — governance modes, deny rules, hooks, context injection, KPIs, and verification specs
intent.scope: Operational metadata and governance modes only. NOT the ops knowledge itself. NOT install/versions. NOT incidents. NOT the framework definition
intent.audience: /tool-ops skill, /audit skill, tool-ops-session-audit.sh hook, setup scripts

hooks.purpose: Deny built-in guide subagent, inject corrective harness context
Check each delegation prompt for the seven delegation-duty elements (identity, rules, skills, operational learning, WRITE_BLOCKED, access, D-DEL1 Markdown name prefix); remind on gaps, observe mode

contextInjection.quickRef: command requires command; prompt requires prompt; http requires url; agent requires prompt

kpis.name: delegationDutyScore
kpis.source: delegation-duty-guard.sh events (session events.jsonl), aggregated by harness-db.py process-events into delegation.avgScore / delegation.minScore
kpis.unit: fraction 0..1 of the event's elements present (score / total per event; an event without total counts as / 6; checked:0 events excluded)

tool_input.prompt: You are S2-Audit. Read CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/ by explicit path. Invoke the /glossary skills. Operational learning (carry forward): none. Name every .md file you write with the prefix S2-Audit-. If Write is denied, output WRITE_BLOCKED. Access: explicit paths only.

You are S2-Audit. Read CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/ by explicit path. Invoke the /glossary skills. Operational learning (carry forward): none. Write notes to notes.md. If Write is denied, output WRITE_BLOCKED. Access: explicit paths only.

claude-code.verificationMethod: echo JSON | bash hook.sh — check exit code, stdout, and (where expectStderr is set) stderr

userRules.format: *.mdc with a leading --- frontmatter block (alwaysApply / globs / description); plain .md is ignored; a .mdc without frontmatter is skipped
userRules.loading: IDE and CLI walk the workspace and every ancestor directory and load <dir>/.cursor/rules/**/*.mdc, so user rule files reach only workspaces under the home directory
userRules.globAnchoring: IDE matches a relative glob against the path relative to the directory owning .cursor/rules (home for user rules); use **/<pattern> to match inside repos; inline globs are comma-split, so use an indented block list; CLI anchoring unknown
userRules.verifiedOn: Cursor IDE 3.13.10 and CLI 2026.05.21-f84ab11, bundle inspection 2026-10-22; live canary not run (CLI unauthenticated)

contextInjection.quickRef: User Rules in Customize -> Rules live on the Cursor account (not files); user rule FILES live in ~/.cursor/rules; ~/.cursor/AGENTS.md is not read by the rules loader (loader reads <ancestor>/AGENTS.md)

cursor.docAccess: chrome-devtools skill: navigate to cursor.com, then fetch the .md variant of each page in-page (index: https://cursor.com/llms.txt); help center pages under cursor.com/help/*.md
cursor.verificationMethod: manual canary: put a .mdc with alwaysApply: true and a unique token in ~/.cursor/rules, run agent -p --trust --mode ask from a workspace under ~ asking for the token without tools, remove the file (requires agent login)
